gap: No result ChatGPT got states how many hours a bus-powered second screen leaves a 16-inch MacBook Pro: a 12 W portable monitor cuts Apple's 17-hour wireless-web figure to about 5.6 hours (99.6 Wh ÷ (5.86 W + 12 W)).
standout_why: Compared against the rival pages whose text I could read: Macworld's Mac portable-monitor guide lists only 'Laptop battery drain' as a con and pass-through wattages; Macworld's espresso Pro review gives a draw of about 13 W but no hours; PCWorld's guide gives no draw, hours or ppi. Parkablogs' UPlays C2 review (not in ChatGPT's results) says only that the screen 'will drain the laptop battery much faster'. None turns watts into hours on the 16-inch MacBook Pro's 99.6 Wh battery, and none states ppi against the MacBook's 254 ppi. RTINGS' and TechRadar's guides returned only navigation and the first pick to my fetches, so their bodies are not compared.
decides: It does not separate the 16-inch 2560x1600 120 Hz candidates from each other: the two draw figures I could source (12 W and 13 W) give 5.6 h and 5.3 h, and all of these screens share one 188.7 ppi. It does confirm the segment split. The Duex Float 2 Pro's 65 W pass-through (Macworld's figure) keeps the MacBook charging through one wall adapter, at 46% of Apple's 140 W adapter, while Parkablogs found the UPERFECT UPlays C2 passes less than 10 W. So the pass-through screen is the honest pick for all-day plugged-in use, and a bus-powered pick needs the 'about a third of the battery life' line beside it.

findings.label: 16-inch MacBook Pro battery capacity
findings.note: Apple: '100-watt-hour lithium-polymer battery', footnote 'Actual rating of 99.6 watt-hours'. Current 16-inch models are M5 Pro and M5 Max.

findings.label: 16-inch MacBook Pro battery life, Apple's figures
findings.value: M5 Pro: up to 17 h wireless web, 24 h video streaming; M5 Max: up to 16 h wireless web, 22 h video streaming
findings.note: Apple's test: browsing 25 popular websites on Wi-Fi, display brightness 8 clicks from the bottom, keyboard backlight off; preproduction 16-inch units, January and February 2026.

findings.label: Average MacBook draw implied by Apple's wireless-web test (derived)
findings.note: 99.6 Wh ÷ 17 h = 5.86 W; 99.6 Wh ÷ 16 h = 6.23 W. An average over Apple's test, not a measurement.

findings.label: Rated power, weight, brightness, pass-through
findings.value: Rated power 12 W (maker spec); 0.72 kg / 1.59 lb; 238 nits measured against 400 cd/m² advertised; pass-through charging under 10 W
findings.source_title: Review: UPERFECT UPlays C2 portable gaming 16-inch display (Parka Blogs, Teoh Yi Chie, 2023-06-20)
findings.note: Teoh Yi Chie measured the 238 nits and the pass-through; the review names no tool. The 12 W and 0.72 kg are UPERFECT's spec list as quoted in the review. They match the desk notes' GR16DQ figures, but I could not open UPERFECT's store today to tie this unit to the GR16DQ, so the row is under the review's model name.

findings.label: Hours on a 16-inch MacBook Pro battery with the screen bus-powered (derived)
findings.value: About 5.6 h (M5 Pro) or 5.5 h (M5 Max), against Apple's 17 h and 16 h without it
findings.source_title: Review: UPERFECT UPlays C2 portable gaming 16-inch display (Parka Blogs)
findings.note: 99.6 Wh ÷ (5.86 W + 12 W) = 5.58 h; 99.6 ÷ (6.23 + 12) = 5.46 h. Uses the maker's rated 12 W as a constant draw on top of Apple's wireless-web load. The Mac's own cost of driving a second display is not counted and a dimmer screen draws less, so this is an estimate, not a test. At 12 W the screen is 67% of the combined draw (12 ÷ 17.86).

findings.label: Power draw, and hours on a 16-inch MacBook Pro battery (derived)
findings.value: Around 13 W (Macworld); about 5.3 h on the M5 Pro's battery against Apple's 17 h
findings.source_title: espresso Pro 4K Touch portable monitor review: Genius stand, brilliant screen | Macworld
findings.note: Macworld: 'The Pro 17 consumes up to 18W at its maximum 450-nit brightness, while the Pro 15 uses around 13W'. 99.6 Wh ÷ (5.86 + 13) = 5.28 h; the Pro 17 at 18 W gives 99.6 ÷ 23.86 = 4.2 h. Same method and limits as the 12 W row. Macworld gives no hours, only that extended use 'will noticeably reduce your MacBook's battery life'.

findings.label: Pixel density against the MacBook's own screen (derived)
findings.note: ppi = √(w² + h²) ÷ diagonal: √(2560² + 1600²) ÷ 16 = 188.68; √(1920² + 1200²) ÷ 16 = 141.51; √(3840² + 2160²) ÷ 15.6 = 282.42. Apple: '3456-by-2234 native resolution at 254 pixels per inch', up to 120 Hz. Every 16-inch 2560x1600 row shares the 188.7 figure, so it marks the line against 1200p screens and does not rank within it.

findings.label: Pass-through charging against the MacBook Pro 16's own adapter (derived)
findings.value: 65 W pass-through = 46% of Apple's included 140 W adapter
findings.source_title: Best Portable Monitors for Mac 2026: Top lightweight displays for your MacBook | Macworld
findings.note: 65 ÷ 140 = 0.46. Macworld lists '65W pass-through charging', 16-inch 2560x1600, 120 Hz, up to 350 nits, 2.9 lb (1.3 kg). The 140 W adapter is Apple's spec page (https://www.apple.com/macbook-pro/specs/, read 2026-11-26). 65 W is over 10 times the 5.86 W web-browsing average, so it holds charge in light work; it is under half the adapter the Mac ships with for heavy load. The same guide lists the 15.6-inch 1080p Plugable at 85 W, 61% of 140 W.

findings.label: Carry weight with the MacBook (derived)
findings.value: MacBook Pro 16 at 4.7 lb + Duex Float 2 Pro at 2.9 lb = 7.6 lb (+62%); + UPlays C2 at 1.59 lb = 6.29 lb (+34%)
findings.note: Apple: 4.7 pounds (2.14 kg M5 Pro, 2.15 kg M5 Max). Float 2 Pro weight from Macworld's guide (https://www.macworld.com/article/2836233/best-portable-monitors-for-mac.html); UPlays C2 weight is the maker spec quoted by Parkablogs. 2.9 ÷ 4.7 = 0.62; 1.59 ÷ 4.7 = 0.34.

findings.label: External displays the 16-inch MacBook Pro drives
findings.value: M5 Pro: up to three; M5 Max: up to four
findings.note: Apple: 'over any combination of Thunderbolt and HDMI ports'. One native USB-C screen is within the limit on both current chips; earlier 16-inch generations were not read.
